unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee of a covered employer qualifies as an eligible employee for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); AND (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (subject to § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an employee is absent from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Regarding employee entitlements under 29 CFR 825.110 in relation to USERRA.
unit_attributes.statement: This section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining duration of employment, if an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Intermittent, occasional, or casual employment.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (subject to special rules in § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirements (such as bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked and claims that full-time teachers of an educational establishment who often work outside the classroom or at home are not eligible for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: must be able to clearly demonstrate
unit_attributes.statement: In order to claim that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment are not eligible for FMLA leave when accurate records are not kept, an employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the teachers did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applicable to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where a break in service of more than seven years exists, and one of the qualifying exceptions applies.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence necessitated by such service must also be counted, without providing greater entitlement than USERRA), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining weeks of employment and whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; and for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for determining compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; it is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to be an eligible employee under the FMLA.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding leave commencement, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee had a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence due to USERRA service must also be counted, without granting greater entitlement than USERRA), or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; the determination is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

findings.assessment: High1 retained intermittent/reduced schedules and the qualified August/December example. Both medium runs omitted them from extracted wording. Medium2 scope also combines notice protection with already-started leave, potentially narrowing protection before leave starts.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In ascertaining an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles of the worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave while the employer employs 50 or more employees within 75 miles, even if the employer expects the number of employees to drop below 50 by the time the leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles (such as 60 employees in August), even if the employer expects the number of employees to drop below 50 (such as to 40 in December) for a period of leave to begin in December.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee's leave has already started, or when an employee gives notice of the need for leave.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave; once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice, and an employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee has been determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, and leave has already started.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50 within 75 miles; eligibility is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave and is not affected by subsequent changes in employee headcount for that specific notice.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is not limited by methods of recordkeeping, or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all of the hours an employee has worked for or been in service to the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.

unit_attributes.statement: While employers are not prevented from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to carriage of firearms and other weapons on an individual's person or accessible property if the individual meets one of three specified criteria.
unit_attributes.choice_text: The individual must be one of the following: (1) law enforcement personnel required to carry a firearm or other weapons while in the performance of law enforcement duty at the airport; (2) an individual authorized to carry a weapon in accordance with §§ 1544.219, 1544.221, 1544.223, 1546.211, or subpart B of part 1562 of this chapter; or (3) an individual authorized to carry a weapon in a sterile area under a security program.
unit_attributes.statement: Paragraph (a) of this section does not apply as to carriage of firearms and other weapons if the individual is: (1) law enforcement personnel required to carry a firearm or other weapons while in the performance of law enforcement duty at the airport; (2) an individual authorized to carry a weapon in accordance with §§ 1544.219, 1544.221, 1544.223, 1546.211, or subpart B of part 1562 of this chapter; or (3) an individual authorized to carry a weapon in a sterile area under a security program.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In checked baggage or in baggage carried in an inaccessible cargo hold under § 1562.23 of this chapter, governing any unloaded firearm(s) unless all four declaration, condition, packaging, and locking requirements are met.
unit_attributes.choice_text: The declaration to the aircraft operator may be made either orally or in writing.
unit_attributes.statement: A passenger may not transport or offer for transport in checked baggage or in baggage carried in an inaccessible cargo hold under § 1562.23 of this chapter any unloaded firearm(s) unless: (i) the passenger declares to the aircraft operator, either orally or in writing, before checking the baggage, that the passenger has a firearm in his or her bag and that it is unloaded; (ii) the firearm is unloaded; (iii) the firearm is carried in a hard-sided container; and (iv) the container in which it is carried is locked, and only the passenger retains the key or combination.

unit_attributes.scope_text: As to carriage of firearms and other weapons on an individual's person or accessible property, if the individual is one of the listed categories.
unit_attributes.choice_text: The individual must be one of the following: (1) Law enforcement personnel required to carry a firearm or other weapons while in the performance of law enforcement duty at the airport; (2) An individual authorized to carry a weapon in accordance with §§ 1544.219, 1544.221, 1544.223, 1546.211, or subpart B of part 1562 of this chapter; or (3) An individual authorized to carry a weapon in a sterile area under a security program.
unit_attributes.statement: Paragraph (a) of 49 CFR 1540.111 does not apply to the carriage of firearms and other weapons if the individual is law enforcement personnel required to carry a weapon in the performance of duty at the airport, an individual authorized to carry a weapon under §§ 1544.219, 1544.221, 1544.223, 1546.211, or subpart B of part 1562, or an individual authorized to carry a weapon in a sterile area under a security program.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In checked baggage or in baggage carried in an inaccessible cargo hold under § 1562.23 of this chapter, unless all specified declaration, unloading, hard-sided container, and locking requirements are met.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All of the following must be met: (i) The passenger declares to the aircraft operator, either orally or in writing, before checking the baggage, that the passenger has a firearm in his or her bag and that it is unloaded; (ii) The firearm is unloaded; (iii) The firearm is carried in a hard-sided container; and (iv) The container in which it is carried is locked, and only the passenger retains the key or combination.
unit_attributes.statement: A passenger may not transport or offer for transport in checked baggage or in baggage carried in an inaccessible cargo hold under § 1562.23 of this chapter any unloaded firearm(s) unless the passenger declares it orally or in writing before checking baggage, the firearm is unloaded, the firearm is carried in a hard-sided container, and the container is locked with only the passenger retaining the key or combination.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises
unit_attributes.choice_text: all of the following conditions
unit_attributes.statement: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises, the organizer must satisfy all of the following conditions: illuminate every public exit throughout the time the display remains open; keep every public exit clear throughout the time the display remains open; appoint an adult steward who remains on site throughout the time the display remains open (unless an agency employee is assigned to supervise for that entire period); and give the agency a qualifying inspection record before admitting the first visitor.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises, before admitting the first visitor
unit_attributes.choice_text: either a signed paper inspection record or an electronic inspection record signed by the inspecting officer
unit_attributes.statement: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises, before admitting the first visitor, the organizer must give the agency either a signed paper inspection record or an electronic inspection record signed by the inspecting officer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When a storm warning is active, unless all of the following conditions are met: the demonstration takes place beneath a fixed roof; the agency has measured wind speed below 20 kilometers per hour at the demonstration site within the preceding 10 minutes; and an agency officer authorizes the demonstration for the duration of the current warning
unit_attributes.choice_text: all of the following conditions
unit_attributes.statement: When a storm warning is active, the organizer must suspend outdoor demonstrations unless all of the following conditions are met: (1) the demonstration takes place beneath a fixed roof; (2) the agency has measured wind speed below 20 kilometers per hour at the demonstration site within the preceding 10 minutes; and (3) an agency officer authorizes the demonstration for the duration of the current warning.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an agency officer authorizes an outdoor demonstration during an active storm warning
unit_attributes.statement: An agency officer's authorization of an outdoor demonstration during an active storm warning expires when that warning ends, and does not authorize demonstrations under a later warning.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For displays held entirely before sunset
unit_attributes.statement: For displays held entirely before sunset, the organizer should place a readable map near the entrance.

unit_attributes.scope_text: After the display closes
unit_attributes.statement: The organizer must retain each inspection record for at least 30 calendar days after the display closes.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an investigation is open when the 30-calendar-day retention period ends after the display closes
unit_attributes.statement: If an investigation is open when the 30-calendar-day retention period ends after the display closes, the organizer must retain the record until the agency closes the investigation.
Visitors are not required to supply their home addresses.
This policy does not prohibit visitors from bringing paper maps.
Other premises rules may restrict particular materials brought by visitors.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When several groups arrive together
unit_attributes.statement: A queue may form when several groups arrive together.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking FMLA eligibility.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (referencing § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in section 825.110 prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's requirement that a record be kept of their hours worked (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees as defined in 29 CFR part 541).
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked, in order to claim that an employee (such as a full-time teacher) is not eligible for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate, for example, that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the teachers are not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start (referencing § 825.300(b) for employee eligibility notice rules).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employee meets the 12-month eligibility requirement while on non-FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to ascertaining whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles for an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, for that specific notice of the need for leave.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles, but the employer expects the count to drop below 50 by the time leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles (e.g., 60 employees in August) for a period of leave to begin later (e.g., in December), even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three criteria must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees who work outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months and the employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541).
unit_attributes.modality_quote: must be able to clearly demonstrate
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (such as full-time teachers defined in § 825.102 who often work outside the classroom or at home) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave (referencing § 825.300(b) for rules governing eligibility notices).

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to that notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer employs 50 or more employees at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, but expects the employee count to drop below 50 before the leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when the 50-employee threshold is met, even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 before the leave is scheduled to begin (for example, employing 60 employees in August when notice is given for leave to begin in December when the employee count is expected to drop to 40).

findings.assessment: Conditions still do not consistently survive into each standalone field. High1 nonconsecutive-month prose embeds adjacent optional-counting text awkwardly; high2 statement preserves a general proviso but scope drops it. Prior-service permission omits mandatory uniform treatment in both; accurate-accounting permission omits c2/aircrew exception context in both. Larger effort is no proof of independently complete rule meanings.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted, subject to paragraph (b)(2) exceptions.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in section 825.110 prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), with the determining factor being the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is not limited by methods of recordkeeping, or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all of the hours an employee has worked for or been in service to the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining actual hours worked under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the counting of prior employment periods complies with the rules governing breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785); the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, and the determination is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all hours worked or in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All of the following conditions: (1) illuminate every public exit throughout the time the display remains open; (2) keep every public exit clear throughout the time the display remains open; (3) appoint an adult steward who remains on site throughout the time the display remains open (unless an agency employee is assigned to supervise for that entire period); and (4) before admitting the first visitor, give the agency either a signed paper inspection record or an electronic inspection record signed by the inspecting officer, with each record identifying the display, the inspection date, and every public exit inspected.
unit_attributes.statement: For a temporary display open to the public after sunset on agency premises, the organizer must satisfy all of the following conditions: illuminate every public exit throughout the time the display remains open; keep every public exit clear throughout the time the display remains open; appoint an adult steward who remains on site throughout the time the display remains open (unless an agency employee is assigned to supervise the display for that entire period); and, before admitting the first visitor, give the agency either a signed paper inspection record or an electronic inspection record signed by the inspecting officer, identifying the display, the inspection date, and every public exit inspected.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When a storm warning is active, unless all of the following conditions are met: the demonstration takes place beneath a fixed roof; the agency has measured wind speed below 20 kilometers per hour at the demonstration site within the preceding 10 minutes; and an agency officer authorizes the demonstration for the duration of the current warning.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Unless all of the following conditions are met: (1) the demonstration takes place beneath a fixed roof; (2) the agency has measured wind speed below 20 kilometers per hour at the demonstration site within the preceding 10 minutes; and (3) an agency officer authorizes the demonstration for the duration of the current warning.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an agency officer authorizes an outdoor demonstration for the duration of an active storm warning.
